title: Introduce proportional stress sampler and degradation-credit sentinel for canary stabilization
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Adds a proportional traffic sampler for stress probing and a degradation-credit sentinel to reduce noisy rollback flapping; opt-in via canary config
body:
Context and motivation:
We run continuous performance canaries across production-like traffic to detect regressions early. Existing probes are either static (fixed qps) or full-traffic shadows which can misrepresent load or add cost. We also observed noisy rollbacks during short transient degradations. This PR introduces two complementary mechanisms: (1) a proportional stress sampler that injects probe traffic proportionally to recent load patterns (keeps probe representativeness across traffic modes), and (2) a degradation-credit sentinel that requires sustained regression credit accumulation before triggering an automatic rollback, reducing flapping during transient spikes.

What this change does (summary):
- Implement proportional-stress sampler in perf-canary/prober: schedules probes that scale probe volume relative to a traffic fingerprint (by percentile buckets).
- Add degradation-credit sentinel in canary-evaluator: a credit ledger that increments on detected degradation signals and decays over time; only when credits exceed a threshold does it mark a canary as failing.
- Expose config knobs in canary policy YAML: probe.scale_strategy = "proportional", sentinel.credit_window_ms, sentinel.decay_rate
- Add integration tests that simulate traffic mode changes (steady, bursty, low-qps) and validate probe representativeness and sentinel hysteresis behavior.
- Observatory: dashboard panels and alert rule for "sentinel_credit_balance" and a new histogram for probe qps distribution.

Design notes and trade-offs:
- Proportional sampler uses an exponential moving average of recent requests grouped by percentile traffic fingerprints to decide probe multiplier. This keeps the probe mix small in low-traffic tenants but increases probe frequency in heavy-traffic scenarios to preserve statistical power.
- Degradation-credit sentinel intentionally biases towards hysteresis: short regressions add limited credit which decays quickly; sustained regressions accumulate faster. This dampens rollbacks for noisy metrics while still enabling response to true sustained regressions.
- Both features are opt-in and default to off for existing customers. They are exposed as canary policy fields and default values are conservative.

Checklist (what I changed):
- [x] Implementation in prober scheduler and canary-evaluator core
- [x] Unit tests for credit ledger and sampler heuristics
- [x] Integration test harness with synthetic traffic patterns
- [x] Docs: canary policy reference and runbook note
- [x] Dashboard panels and Grafana queries + example thresholds
- [x] Feature flag gating + migration note

Commits included (high-level):
- 9f7a2b1: add proportional stress sampler core loop and configuration parsing
- c3d4e8f: implement degradation-credit ledger and evaluation hook
- b12f44a: integration tests: traffic-mode simulator and synth driver
- e9a0b7e: dashboard queries and grafana JSON export (trimmed)
- f4512c0: docs: canary policy reference and runbook guidance

Files changed (high-level):
- perf-canary/prober/sampler.go (new): proportional sampler implementation and unit tests in sampler_test.go
- perf-canary/evaluator/sentinel.go (new): credit ledger + evaluation policy
- perf-canary/config/policy_schema.go (mod): add fields for sampler and sentinel
- perf-canary/integration/traffic_simulator.go (new): synthetic traffic modes for tests
- docs/canary_policy.md (mod): reference and examples
- observability/grafana/canary_panels.json (mod): new panels and queries
- .github/workflows/perf-integration.yml (mod): add matrix entry for new integration test runs

Review conversation (high level, single thread):
- Diego Ramirez (requested changes, 2026-02-11): "Nice approach. Two asks: (1) please add a deterministic seed option for the sampler for test reproducibility, (2) I think we should add an upper cap on probe multiplier to avoid accidental runaway in extraordinary spikes."
- Maya Patel (author reply, 2026-02-12): "Thanks Diego — added deterministic seed config and a hard upper bound (default 10x). Also added a safety circuit in the scheduler that rejects >1000 probes/sec for an entire deployment as an emergency cap."
- Hannah Cho (comment, 2026-02-13): "Integration tests look good. One note on metric names: recommend using 'canary/sentinel/credit_balance' to align with existing naming conventions."
- Maya Patel (author reply, 2026-02-14): "Renamed metric and updated dashboards."
- Samir Kumar (approval, 2026-02-15): "Approach validated, tests cover critical cases; LGTM after CI green."

CI and validation details:
- Unit tests: pass (local and CI)
- Integration tests (matrix): initially one flaky test failed under the k8s ephemeral runner (traffic_simulator timing); fixed by adding deterministic seed and extending timeouts in the harness. Final CI run: all checks passed.
- Performance baseline: synthetic run shows median probe CPU overhead increase ~1.8% for heavy tenants, within budget; cost trade-offs documented in the canary policy doc.

Migration and rollout plan:
- Feature gated behind canary.policy.experimental.enable_proportional_sampler (default false)
- Rollout plan: enable for internal perf lab tenants first, monitor sentinel_credit_balance and rollback events for 72h, then opt-in for customers with dedicated capacity.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: misconfigured multipliers could overload clusters. Mitigation: hard caps, safety circuit, config validation at admission time.
- Risk: sentinel threshold tuning might be conservative or too permissive. Mitigation: default conservative thresholds, canary-specific overrides, dashboards and alerting for tuning.

Merge details:
- Merge method: squash
- After merging, I kicked off the internal perf lab job to validate a 24h window across three traffic modes; results were as expected and no rollbacks were auto-triggered in the presence of transient spikes.

Notes for reviewers and ops: the canary runbook section at docs/canary_policy.md contains sample YAML snippets and monitoring queries. If you want to exercise the feature locally: perf-canary/integration/README.md includes a short guide to run the traffic simulator with deterministic seeds.
